content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in bullish event windows, indicating a lag in adjusting to supply-demand shifts.", "Sentiment spikes during auction periods correlate with price overshoots, suggesting sentiment amplifies model bias.", "Model forecasts exhibit mean-reversion bias when official supply net is negative, underestimating sharp declines.", "High bullish sentiment events with low supply net trigger forecast overcorrection, leading to premature price peaks.", "Forecast accuracy deteriorates when sentiment is mixed, indicating sentiment interaction undermines model stability.", "Model forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to supply net when bullish sentiment exceeds 25%, suggesting sentiment dominates supply signals.", "Price corrections following auction events are often underestimated by models, indicating forecast lag in capturing exogenous supply shocks.", "Sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., 0.00 to 1.00 transitions) correlates with forecast divergence, suggesting sentiment is a key correction trigger."]}
